html/browsers/origin/cross-origin-object: Jint false pass: the Jint adapter creates the functions of the bindings with the intrinsics of the first realm, so the functions and the accessors of a cross-origin Window or Location had the Function.prototype of the test page by accident. The specification requires a function per caller realm (crossOriginPropertyDescriptorMap), which is not implemented: the new engine returns the functions of the realm of the window.
content-security-policy/reporting-api/re: Jint false pass: the image is fetched by a microtask after the script ends, and Jint still reported the last node of the script as the running location. The new engine reports no location when no script runs, as the specification says (the browsers capture the location when the src attribute is set).
service-workers/service-worker/fetch-eve: Fails with both engines (respondWith() with a body stream that has an invalid chunk is not supported). The harness status is TIMEOUT instead of ERROR: the unhandled rejection of the fetch of the iframe is reported to the iframe, as the specification says, not to the test page.
IndexedDB/structured-clone.any.js*: Implementation-defined output: the names of the Date subtests contain Date.prototype.toString(), whose time zone name is "(Coordinated Universal Time)" with the new engine (as in Chrome) and "(UTC)" with Jint, so the subtests have other names.
